newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Guam renews 1997/98 fuel oil, gas oil contracts.
newsitem.headline: Guam renews 1997/98 fuel oil, gas oil contracts.

text.p: Guam Power Authority (GPA) has decided to renew its existing fuel oil and gas oil import contracts to 1997/1998 and would issue a tender soon for another gas oil contract, GPA's general manager said on Friday.

Randy Wiegand said, subject to final approval by GPA's board of directors, its fuel oil contract with Daxin Petroleum Pte Ltd would be renewed for another year, starting from October 1, 1997 to September 31, 1998.

The renewed deal would be under the same terms as the existing contract in which GPA takes at least 2.7 million barrels of 2.0 percent sulphur fuel oil and 300,000 barrels of the 1.19-percent sulphur grade.

The price for the 2.0-percent sulphur grade would be maintained at a $2.23-per-barrel premium to Singapore's spot 3.5-percent sulphur fuel oil quotes and the 1.19-percent sulphur grade at a $3.15-premium, both on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis.
GPA will also renew its 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil contracts with Shell and Mobil with each retaining the current 15-million-gallon volumes.
Shell's price was a premium of 7.94 cents per gallon to Singapore spot quotes, while Mobil's price was a 7.63-cent premium, both on a c-and-f basis.
Wiegand said for future contracts, GPA would seek a two-to-three-year term period, instead of the current one-year duration, with the option for renewal.
"We don't want to go through the hassle and uncertainty of having to renew annual contracts," he said.

Wiegand also said GPA will issue another term tender sometime in September or October for a new contract to supply 15 million to 20 million gallons of 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil to a new power station on the Pacific island.
The 40-megawatt power station, belonging to Taiwan Electric and Mechanical Engineering Services, is scheduled to start up in November or December.
The first cargo is expected to be delivered from end October, he said.
GPA would also seek a two-to-three-year delivery period for this contract, Wiegand said.
GPA has sealed a 20-year gas oil supply contract with Taiwan Electric in September 1996.
